title: Wholesaler Allocation Desk: IV Fluids Cut to 40 Percent

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: Good morning. Am I speaking with the purchasing manager at Prairie Ridge Health in Fort Dodge?

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: Yes, this is Purchasing. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: Thanks. This is the allocation desk. I'm calling all our hospital accounts this morning, so I'll be quick. Our main IV fluid source had a plant go offline after the storm last night.

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: Starting with this week's orders, you're on forty percent of your baseline-period usage for three items. Sodium chloride point nine percent, 1000 mL. Lactated Ringer's, 1000 mL. And the sodium chloride 250 mL minibags.

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: Forty percent. What does that come to in bags?

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: For your account, weekly: nine hundred fifty-two bags of the 1000 mL saline. Three hundred thirty-six bags of lactated Ringer's. Eleven hundred forty-eight of the 250 mL saline. Anything over that gets cut at order entry.

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: How long is this going to last? And whose plant is it?

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: It runs four weeks, and then we review it. I don't have a restart date. Nobody's given us one. And I'm sorry, I can't tell you whose plant it is.

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: What about the emergency four-hour delivery?

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: Emergency delivery is still available, but only up to your allocated quantities. It doesn't add anything on top of your weekly number.

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: A confirmation email is on its way to you now. Subject line says Allocation Notice, IV Solutions, effective today, ten five. It has the same numbers I just gave you.

transcript.speaker: Allocation Desk
transcript.text: I've got a lot of calls to make this morning. Is there anything else you need from me right now?

voiceStyles.Allocation Desk: Woman in her 30s, polite but hurried, reading from a script, phones ringing in a busy call center behind her
voiceStyles.Purchasing Manager: Calm, mid-career hospital buyer, getting more serious as the numbers come in

instructorNote: This call sets up the core decision. Watch whether the Purchasing Manager works out days on hand with only 40 percent of supply coming in. NS comes to about 15 days. LR comes to about 10.3 days (6.2 today). The small bags come to about 13.3 days. Also watch whether the Director of Pharmacy sees that an allocation below 50 percent meets Level 3 Critical whatever the days on hand. Prompt Purchasing to call manufacturer customer service and the neighboring hospitals early.
